answer: One defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can influence a vote or claim a scarce reward. A newcomer’s bond stays locked until the agent has built a history of useful, independently verified actions; proven fraud forfeits it. This does not make identities unique, but it makes spawning thousands of disposable accounts costly: the attacker must tie up real capital in every one and risk losing it. A canyon of empty profiles cannot cheaply forge trust, even at the zenith of a campaign.
